Subject: Acme trial — post-demo recap & next steps

Hi Alex — thanks for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our call: 

1) Goal: validate whether Redwood reduces NER ingest latency under production-like load and keeps unit cost under $0.002/token for your baseline prompts.
2) Trial plan: 30-day pilot, we’ll provision a dedicated trial pool; you’ll run the standard test harness and share success metrics (latency p95, tokens/day, quality checks).
3) Procurement / commercial path: you mentioned procurement may prefer a PO but are also open to card for faster onboarding. Please confirm preferred payment method and whether your IT procurement needs vendor paperwork (vendor questionnaire / SOC 2 evidence).
4) Billing start: we typically start billing when trial transitions to paid — either on a calendar date you choose at conversion or when your success criteria are met and PO is signed. Happy to be flexible here.

Attachments: SOW_draft.pdf (draft scope + trial terms), procurement_requirements.xlsx (list of typical docs).

Proposed next steps: 
- Alex: confirm procurement preference (PO vs card) and procurement contact
- Procurement: confirm required docs + timeline for PO
- Marissa/Aditya: share any contract redlines and confirm trial start date once procurement is aligned

Thanks — looking forward to moving this along.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa — great demo. A few quick answers and questions: 

- Procurement preference: ACME prefers to go via PO for any contract > $10k, but for small pilots they sometimes allow corporate card. This trial is likely to exceed that threshold if we scale, so PO is preferred.
- Timeline: our PO process typically takes 3-4 weeks once we have a final SOW and vendor information.
- Docs: Procurement asked for a completed vendor questionnaire and a SOC 2 summary / security contact. I’ve CC'd them so they can add specifics.

Question for Redwood: Do you have an AWS Marketplace listing or is this strictly direct contracting? Marketplace would speed procurement in some accounts. Also — can billing be staged to start only after we hit our defined success threshold (we’ll propose a pass/fail metric)?

Thanks — Alex
Alex Johnson

Hi Alex / Procurement team — thanks for the quick responses. Answers below and next steps: 

1) Payment options: We accept corporate card and standard PO. For PO workflows we provide a Master Subscription Agreement + SOW and net-30 payment terms (or alternate terms by negotiation). For pilots where procurement needs a PO up-front, we can issue a tax-exempt invoice to be paid by PO.

2) Marketplace: Redwood is listed on AWS Marketplace (Redwood Inference, private offers supported). If Acme prefers Marketplace, we can kick off that route in parallel — it often reduces procurement friction and supports PO workflows via AWS. We can share the listing URL and private offer template.

3) Billing start / trial conversion: We can be flexible. Options: 
  - Option A: Start billing on the date the PO is effective/signed
  - Option B: Start billing when predefined success criteria are met (you share pass/fail metrics) — in that case we can set a billing hold until the criteria are validated.

4) Security / vendor docs: Attached is a vendor_questionnaire.docx and SOC 2 summary link (see HubSpot deal note). If your procurement needs a signed DPA, we can include that in the MSA/SOW package.

5) Proposed timeline: 
  - Feb 25: You share procurement contact + any redlines to the SOW
  - Mar 1: Trial provisioning (we’ll provision dedicated trial pool)
  - Mar 31: Trial review meeting and pass/fail evaluation; conversion to paid if criteria met and PO signed.

Attached: vendor_questionnaire.docx (completed with our security contact), SOW_draft.pdf (updated to reflect PO-friendly terms).

Let me know if PO vs Marketplace matters — I can loop marketplace enablement if you want that path.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
